tag.description: The knowledge stream this belongs to, declared by the emitting node. A sweep seeds from the same tag it emits to.

dedupeKey.description: Cross-run identity, built from the node's own dedupe fields. Two runs finding the same thing produce the same key.

claim.description: What was found, in the finder's words. A lesson without a claim is a row nobody can act on.

status.description: Whether the panel let it stand. Killed lessons are the valuable half: they are what a later sweep would otherwise re-argue from scratch.

objection.description: The strongest refuter objection recorded against it — for a killed lesson, why it died; for a survivor, the best case still against it.

kills.description: Refuters that voted to kill, out of the panel that judged it.

provenance.description: The recorded run this came from. Required, and checked against runs/ on append: a lesson with no run behind it is an assertion, and this file only holds findings.

supersededBy.description: Present when an earlier row already held this identity. Supersession appends; nothing here is ever rewritten. Carries the filing run's own id, so it reads as a flag rather than a count — `arrivals` is the number.

classKey.description: Coarse identity: the defect's SHAPE rather than its location. Declared by the emitting node as memory.classBy and never inferred, because a class guessed from claim similarity collapses unrelated lessons and a gate that fires on everything gets skimmed. Absent when the node declared none.

arrivals.description: Distinct runs that have filed this tag|dedupeKey, this one included. Carried forward onto every new row: the claim is latest-state-wins, the count is not.

classArrivals.description: Distinct runs that have filed anything in this tag|classKey. This is the number that survives a consolidation restating two identities as one, and the one a recurrence gate acts on.

firstSeen.description: establishedWhen of the oldest row under this identity, carried forward. How long the thing has been known, which supersession used to erase.
